subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a contained conditional statement is terminated by the termination or next phrase of a containing statement; 'Any phrase encountered is the next phrase of the most-recently preceding unterminated statement with which that phrase may be syntactically associated. If all permitted occurrences of a phrase have already been specified for a given statement, a subsequent occurrence of that phrase is not syntactically associated with that statement' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 4)). Mechanism (kb/Work PB3830): every Table 12 [NOT] phrase of every statement is the ONE conditionalPhrases rule, whose context-dependent predicate ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Associates admits a phrase to a statement exactly when one of its printed general formats takes it beside the phrases already written and it is not already written; ANTLR's greedy loop asks the innermost open statement first and returns outward otherwise - the rule's association order (ifStatement's single ELSE does the same for THEN/ELSE). The paragraph is cited as 14.5.3.3 (it follows list item 4 unindented on the rendered page; cite.py labels it 4)). Probes: nested IFs, second ELSE goes to the outer IF (sc1 T6 'T6 OUTER-ELSE', T6B 'T6B INNER-ELSE'); END-IF-terminated inner IF lets ELSE go outer (sc1 T7); ADD conditional inside IF ended by ELSE (sc1 T9); SEARCH inside IF ended by ELSE, both WHENs to SEARCH (sc4 U6 'U6 FOUND'); exhausted inner NOT ON SIZE ERROR passes the second NOT to the outer ADD (sc1 T1/T2). The golden's S1/S3 pin association and the 'already matched with an ELSE' exhaustion for IF. Reach note: §14.5.1 makes a conditional statement imperative only when delimited, and every Table-12 conditional phrase and EVALUATE/PERFORM body is written imperative-statement-n, so in a CONFORMING program the only containing statement a conditional can sit in unterminated is IF (§14.9.19.2 statement-1/-2), whose only later phrase is ELSE. Since kb/Work PB3830 the association follows the printed formats, so a READ's INVALID KEY beside its AT END, a WRITE's INVALID KEY beside END-OF-PAGE, a CALL's NOT ON OVERFLOW and a second occurrence of a phrase associate with no statement (COBOL2269 names them), and CALL's ON OVERFLOW associates only at an edition that prints it (85-2014), so at 2023 it is the enclosing STRING's. The PB3830 goldens pin each family: the inner statement takes the phrase and is refused COBOL2796 (both orders), the outer statement takes a phrase the inner cannot (pb3830_phrase_association legs 1-6), and a same-verb nest whose inner END- closes the inner statement leaves the outer phrase running to the period (legs 7-8, which the outward reading would print differently). probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY (test-needed) — Implementation conforms: adjudicator sc1 T6 (IF IF ELSE ELSE, second ELSE to outer), refuter R2 (ELSE terminates a contained undelimited EVALUATE, both truth values), R3 (ELSE terminates contained READ AT END/NOT AT END), R8, E5 (third ELSE with both IFs exhausted rejected COBOL0307). But the golden does not pin the rule load-bearing branches: branch b) "next phrase of any containing statement" terminating a contained CONDITIONAL, and the exhaustion sentence, are never reached - in S2/S3/S4 every inner IF is END-IF terminated before the ELSE (so S3 is decided by the END-IF, not by the already-matched-ELSE exhaustion the adjudicator credits it with), and in S1 the inner IF is ended by the period. Only the association sentence (S1 dangling ELSE) is pinned. A deciding test: IF T IF F DISPLAY 1 ELSE DISPLAY 2 ELSE DISPLAY 3. with no END-IF (expect 2), plus IF F IF .. ELSE .. ELSE DISPLAY 3. (expect 3).
